subject: Errors in sampler selection leads to failed MCMC

messages.author: b5e081313b0902ca
messages.subject: Errors in sampler selection leads to failed MCMC
parts:
Hi all,

Sorry for the two posts in two days.

I am trying to run the following model, which compiles fine but gives an error in the MCMC. 

code <- nimbleCode({
  for(j in 1:p){
    w[1:n, j] ~ dmnorm(zeroes[1:n], cov = cov[1:n, 1:n])
  }
  for(i in 1:n){
    y[i, 1:p] ~ dmnorm(w[i, 1:p], cov = Omega[1:p, 1:p])
  }
})

# constants
{
  cov <- structure(c(1, 0.291439908378029, 0.944925896806776, 0.291439908378029,
                     1, 0.278127103103443, 0.944925896806776, 0.278127103103443, 1
  ), dim = c(3L, 3L))
  n <- 3; p <- 2
 
  constants <- list(Omega = diag(1,p),
                    zeroes = rep(0, n),
                    p = p,
                    n = n,
                    cov = cov)
 
}

jsdmModel <- nimbleModel(code,
                         constants = constants)

jsdmModel$setData(list(y = matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)))

jsdmcompiled <- compileNimble(jsdmModel, resetFunctions = T)
jsdmConf <- configureMCMC(jsdmcompiled, print = TRUE,
                          enableWAIC = T)
jsdmMCMC <- buildMCMC(jsdmConf)
CDNAMCMC <- compileNimble(jsdmMCMC)
MCMCsamples <- runMCMC(CDNAMCMC, niter = 10000, WAIC = T)

The last step gives the error:
Run-time size error: expected dim(prior_prec)[1] == dim(contribution_mean)[1]
Error in mapCopy.  Sizes don't match: 3 != 2

I am not an expert, but I think that the error comes from the selected sampler for w[1:n,j], since it comes out as conjugate even though it shouldn't be.

Indeed, by removing the sampler for w and replacing it with single RW samplers, the error disappears.

jsdmConf$removeSamplers("w")
jsdmConf$addSampler(target = "w[1,1]", type = "RW")
jsdmConf$addSampler(target = "w[2,1]", type = "RW")
jsdmConf$addSampler(target = "w[1,2]", type = "RW")
jsdmConf$addSampler(target = "w[2,2]", type = "RW")
jsdmConf$addSampler(target = "w[3,1]", type = "RW")
jsdmConf$addSampler(target = "w[3,2]", type = "RW")

Is it a bug of Nimble or am I doing something wrong?

Thanks in advance,

Alex

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Errors in sampler selection leads to failed MCMC
parts:
Alex, apologies for the delay in getting back to your question.

This is an interesting case about multivariate normal conjugacy.  nimble's conjugacy detection routine mis-diagnoses this, as a result of the dmnorm prior being declared on the first dimension of the w array (w[1:n, ]), and the dmnorm likelihood being declared on the second dimension of the w array (w[i, 1:p]).  As I said, this case is mis-diagnosed, and attempts to apply nimble's dmnorm-dmnorm conjugate sampler in a case it was not designed to handle.

We'll issue a patch for this, so that the conjugate sampler is not assigned here, and we'll let you know when that's ready to try out.  But in the meantime your best bets are:

(1) If conjugacy isn't needed anywhere else in the MCMC, then simply disable the conjugacy system at the time of MCMC configuration:

jsdmConf <- configureMCMC(jsdmcompiled, print = TRUE, enableWAIC = TRUE, useConjugacy = FALSE)

or,

(2) If you need conjugate samplers to be assigned for use on other dimensions of the model, then it's fairly easy to remove the (incorrectly assigned) conjugate sampler from w, then add the (non-conjugate) default samplers to w, which in this case are multivariate RW_block samplers:

jsdmConf <- configureMCMC(jsdmcompiled, print = TRUE, enableWAIC = TRUE)
jsdmConf$removeSampler('w')
jsdmConf$addSampler('w', default = TRUE, useConjugacy = FALSE)

Please let me know if this gets you moving forward for now, and we'll keep in touch about a patch.

Cheers,
Daniel
